# Filmcraft native editing foundation

Clipline reuses Filmcraft's native editor and document. This directory pins a source archive and one combined patch. It does not contain a second timeline model or the evaluation's fixed-split demo process.

The pinned engine changes provide linked native razor/regular trim and committed-only playback/autosave publication. Native times, source handles, effects and history remain authoritative. Exact JSON float parsing preserves framing values through native save/reopen. Schema2 binds gameplay and an optional separate facecam role across shared, landscape and portrait sequences. Gameplay inherits native audio once; facecam adds no audio. Schema1 remains supported. General shared move/insert/reorder/speed commands remain incomplete. Identified unsupported linked timing commands reject explicitly. Do not expose this scope as a complete Clipline editor.

Document-wide validation includes inactive linked owners, complete native role/source/audio bindings and owner revisions. Save/export owners reject malformed linked documents before IO. Recovery copies retain invalid working data, while optional current-project autosave refuses to overwrite the current file with it. `clipline.saveSnapshot` checks the exact working path, native revision and complete linked-owner inventory, then validates and saves a copy in one synchronous native call. It preserves the working path and dirty state. The Clipline checkpoint gateway publishes those opaque bytes through ProjectStore generation CAS; a lost reply remains uncertain and is not retried automatically.

Accepted source-clock words enter through one native `clipline.acceptCaptions` command. It pins the explicit CreatorLibrary transcript revision, validates source/import and all three existing native caption tracks, and groups/maps cues with native clocks. Linked split/trim regenerates those cues in the same undoable edit. Native style/settings and unmanaged cues remain editable; managed text/timing changes require the canonical accepted transcript owner. Missing/interpolated timing, ambiguous audio selection and conflicting unmanaged cues reject. The parent gateway performs full source verification before and after the edit; native import fingerprints alone are not a fresh file hash.

The Session publication owner retains a validated immutable playback project. Invalid raw working data remains recoverable without reaching live playback, and staged command/group data remains private. The engine mixer and UI playback provider use that same boundary.

The native `clipline-creator-kit` workspace helper captures a supported template and creates a separate editable Moment through scratch Sessions. The canonical Python creation service admits exact registered source/template assets, a pinned KitRecord, an explicit layout profile and the current Moment revision. The helper owns native import, clocks, effects/audio and serialization; the service verifies its receipt and publishes the opaque project through ProjectStore. Uncertain process or publication outcomes retain their evidence and require reconciliation. This initial profile supports static illustrative slots and audio settings, with empty Kit properties and Moment overrides. General Kit updates, additional property/assets support and companion creation/open controls remain incomplete.

The dedicated `clipline-export-snapshot` workspace helper captures an immutable native project and full composition settings before rendering. The Python durable owner binds the exact source, Kit, accepted transcript, snapshot and recipe, then independently probes and fully decodes each output before settlement. Existing schema-1 runtime manifests retain the qualified software H.264 recipe. Schema-2 manifests select an explicit software or GPU-Auto recipe; the current Windows GPU-Auto helper successfully uses NVENC encoding but falls back to CPU composition. Both retain native burned captions and AAC 48 kHz stereo. Blocking headless export is absent from the GUI command registry. Explicit runtime configuration binds each tool and the native source identity; it discovers no executable through PATH. Basic dual-output controls are installed; batch/compilation exports and performance work remain incomplete.

An opt-in `--managed-exit` launch binds a per-session manifest and native final-document evidence. Tagged native quit requests use the launch nonce and a fresh request ID. The native Save, Don't Save and Cancel controls record their actual decisions. Final shutdown joins native saving and retains independently decoded saved content plus final memory or discard evidence. These files describe document state; the Python owner separately requires the original parent to be reaped, its Job Object to contain zero processes and its streams to close before canonical publication or guard release. A disappeared control endpoint is availability loss, not proof of process cessation. Foreign or unverifiable ownership remains reconciliation.

## Prepare source

Obtain the exact archive using the endpoint in `pin.json`. This endpoint reconstructs the tag download; the original request URL was not retained. The verified archive hash and its embedded commit establish the accepted input. Keep downloaded source and Cargo targets outside this repository. Preparation checks the complete archive and patch hashes, refuses an existing destination, preflights archive paths, applies the patch with local Git line-ending conversion disabled, and checks each declared patched file hash. It preserves failed attempts for diagnosis.

From the repository root:

```powershell
python scripts/engine/prepare_filmcraft.py --archive <downloaded-source.zip> --patch vendor/filmcraft/clipline-native-edits.patch --pin vendor/filmcraft/pin.json --destination <fresh-source-directory>
```

A `prepared-source.json` receipt certifies source preparation only. Compilation, native command tests, renderer checks and full editor acceptance are separate. Git attributes preserve the patch bytes because its complete hash is part of the pin. The current patch also preserves the qualified native tree's existing CRLF content. Git can report trailing-whitespace warnings for those carriage returns; source preparation checks the exact resulting bytes instead of normalizing the already qualified source.

## Checks and remaining work

The current combined patch reconstructs the exact 1,388-file NVENC export source tree, SHA256 `76bf502a47aa0e043f41f1281e0847ce4dd816af91ed35f8ae0982516fe0c8c5`. Four paths change from the caption-inventory tree: the export helper's manifest/main, its Cargo.lock dependency references, and the native export snapshot recipe/counters. All 710 package versions and checksums remain unchanged. The locked/offline Windows helper build passed; its executable SHA256 is `4a5b9af5a8c963ca3ca46fb12f038b2425e387fe708ff108fc80c8411ef84aa2`. A real captioned 18-second dual-output run passed native completion, full frame probes, full decode and durable settlement. NVENC encoded 1,080 frames per composition; GPU composition produced zero frames and fell back to CPU. The stricter full-acceleration trial therefore remains failed. This source promotion preserves that distinction and does not establish acceptable final performance or rebuild the GUI.

The prior caption-inventory source tree is SHA256 `b6d9507951567d6443f0be31c0338569c8d98fb151f37fc82996f0cb227983fe`. Its only changes from the managed003 tree were time-free caption-track inventory in `sequence.inspect` and its native tests. Three inventory and 21 caption-projection checks passed, followed by the Windows GUI build. The demonstrated GUI executable remains SHA256 `1eeafaecad96cfda927cc0279ddea5e64eaef2ae5fab8e598960acdd9188a226`. Upstream and Cargo.lock were unchanged at that gate. Source reconstruction does not transfer earlier helper or GUI runtime claims to a different binary.

The prior managed-exit003 source passed 21 native engine checks, two selected argument-parser checks and a full Windows GUI build. Root executed the corrected Python owner against that exact GUI: a late edit forced the native Save prompt, Save retained it through automatic shutdown and a fresh native reopen, and the second ordinary close completed cleanly. Separate actual Don't Save, Cancel followed by a new explicit quit, and stopped-waiting followed by Save all passed. All five native GUI scopes reached zero active processes with reaped exit-zero parents and closed streams, without emergency stop. That prior combined patch reconstructed all 1,387 qualified files exactly from the upstream archive. These gates do not establish Save As, direct-window-close recovery, arbitrary editing, caption accuracy, playback budgets or a complete release. Helper binaries retain their separately recorded qualification identities.

The v5 engine base passed 82 focused native checks on Windows GNU: 21 accepted-caption, 44 linked-command, 16 publication-observer and one shared decoder case. The controller read all four final raw logs. The unified Creator Kit/export source then built both helper executables with locked/offline Cargo and passed 31 native factory plus seven native export public API cases. All four metadata/build/test scopes stopped with exit 0 and closed streams. Root independently checked both complete 1,385-file source inventories, all 25 pinned changed files and the two executable hashes before promotion. The lock retains all base packages and adds only the two workspace helpers. Packaged upstream test targets and full upstream CI remain unrun. The external decoder test calls the real shared decoder with the unchanged focused assertions. The linked fixture has an existing unused helper warning; observer panic output is deliberately injected and caught.

The clean v5 Windows GUI now builds and runs through the product session owner. Actual canonical caption correction, native undo/redo, checkpoint save/reopen, rendered captions and dual landscape/portrait exports pass on local footage. Two separate moment projects also reuse one native Kit template, existing caption styles and one registered source; all four exports pass independent probing and full decode. These tests use authored evaluation words and an illustrative layout. They do not establish speech accuracy, complete Creator Kit application, unrestricted linked editing, global resource control, a finished workflow UI or Premiere performance improvement. Exact receipts and unfinished gates remain in the execution ledger.

The installed canonical creation service separately passed a real-media replay in two fresh Python processes. Both Moments reused one immutable KitRecord and registered source/template assets, then preserved nondefault audio settings through native reopen. Its intentionally muted template proves saved settings rather than audible output. The later managed003 GUI has separate build and close/reopen evidence; it does not transfer the earlier GUI's full caption/export qualification. One inherited linked-command test still contains an evaluation-specific output path. Its qualified bytes remain unchanged; that portability debt requires a separate correction and check before portable upstream test qualification.

The unified Creator Kit and export helpers subsequently passed one real four-second landscape/portrait creation/export replay through the durable owner, independent probing, complete decode and SQLite settlement. The factory and five export/tool scopes stopped cleanly with zero remaining durable holds. That sample intentionally mutes audio and contains no accepted transcript. It proves this bounded unified flow, not audible quality, accepted-caption parity, performance or the complete interface. See `docs/evaluation/2026-10-18-native-export-product.md` and the execution ledger for exact hashes, current product checks and evidence boundaries.
